blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this NIPS 2016 paper as a fascinating exploration of applying machine learning to the design of optimization algorithms. The key insight is that just as learned feature representations have outperformed hand-designed ones in machine learning, learned optimizers can outperform hand-designed optimization algorithms like SGD, Adam, or RMSprop. The paper demonstrates that by training an LSTM-based optimizer on a class of problems, it can generalize to unseen problems within that class, achieving state-of-the-art performance and enabling transfer learning across tasks. Colyer emphasizes the elegance of the functional approach, where optimization itself becomes a learned function, and notes the broader implications of machines designing algorithms that surpass human-designed ones.
paper_title: Learning to learn by gradient descent by gradient descent
paper_abstract: The move from hand-designed features to learned features in machine learning has been wildly successful. In spite of this, optimization algorithms are still designed by hand. In this paper we show how the design of an optimization algorithm can be cast as a learning problem, allowing the algorithm to learn to exploit structure in the problems of interest in an automatic way. Our learned algorithms, implemented by LSTMs, outperform generic, hand-designed competitors on the tasks for which they are trained, and also generalize well to new tasks with similar structure. We demonstrate this on a number of tasks, including simple convex problems, training neural networks, and styling images with neural art.
